method: Screened 13 primary repositories across software process, frontend, security, science, ML, video and platform work. Shortlisted by a concrete job, specific source guidance, available examples/testing and clear limits. Popularity is a separate discovery signal. Sponsorship never changes these selections or evaluation outcomes.
coverage: This is a dated editorial shortlist, not a complete market ranking or universal best-skills claim. Author documentation is labelled separately from our own one-pair trial. Source review can be newer than the pinned catalog download.

picks.name: Systematic debugging
picks.job: Finding the cause of a bug
picks.why: A process pick for repeated failed fixes: reproduce the problem, trace where it starts, then test the proposed cause.
picks.evidence: The reviewed source separates investigation, pattern analysis, hypothesis and implementation. The project also maintains skill-behavior test infrastructure.
picks.limits: A documented process and author tests do not show that this skill improves your bug-fix outcome. No new matched debugging trial here.
picks.version_note: Catalog downloads have their own pinned version; inspect before installing.
picks.reason: Start here when fixes keep failing: reproduce the bug and test its cause before changing more code.

picks.name: React best practices
picks.why: A focused reference for request waterfalls, bundle cost and rendering. Useful when the job is a specific performance change rather than a new visual style.
picks.evidence: Vercel’s source organizes rules by impact, with examples and dedicated references. Our 28 October subscription trial returned identical JavaScript: 3 of 3 checks passed with and without the supplied skill reference.
picks.limits: One small task, one pair, inline reference, tools disabled. Native discovery and internal use were not observed. The tie is no evidence of benefit or harm.
picks.version_note: Catalog downloads have their own pinned version; inspect before installing.
picks.reason: For React performance work: tackle request waterfalls, bundle weight and rendering with concrete examples.

picks.name: Skill creator
picks.why: Worth opening when you want to turn a vague instruction file into something you can exercise and compare.
picks.evidence: The author’s skill includes evaluation, comparison and iteration resources in the reviewed repository. That is more concrete than a promise to make every prompt better.
picks.limits: A harness helps run a comparison; it does not validate its grader or prove transfer to a new task. Review the individual folder licence and dependencies.
picks.version_note: Catalog downloads have their own pinned version; inspect before installing.
picks.reason: For improving a skill: turn instructions into a repeatable task, comparison and iteration loop.

picks.name: Supabase
picks.why: For Supabase work, start with the team that maintains the platform. This skill puts changing docs and concrete authorization pitfalls into the workflow.
picks.evidence: Primary maintainer instructions cover RLS, view invokers, session handling and checks after changes. The author describes cross-agent evaluation in its 9 April launch article.
picks.limits: Author-reported evaluation is not an independent result. No Supabase trial was run here; this is a platform-specific pick.
picks.version_note: Catalog downloads have their own pinned version; inspect before installing.
picks.reason: For Supabase projects: use the platform maintainer’s guidance on RLS, sessions and authorization traps.

picks.name: Remotion best practices
picks.why: A good starting point when the output really is a Remotion project: the router points to creation, markup, captions, media and rendering guidance.
picks.evidence: Maintained in Remotion’s own skills repository and linked from the official project-creation docs. The current source routes to task-specific reference files.
picks.limits: A router is not the full implementation. We have not run a paired video trial or established reuse rights from a repository-level licence; inspect the linked folder terms.
picks.version_note: Catalog downloads have their own pinned version; inspect before installing.
picks.reason: For a Remotion film: jump to task-specific guidance on captions, media and rendering.

picks.name: Frontend design
picks.why: Useful as an exploration aid when the brief needs a deliberate visual direction. Bring the real brand, audience and existing work with you.
picks.evidence: The reviewed source asks for an intentional design approach and concrete implementation instead of a generic component dump.
picks.limits: Visual preference needs human review. This is not an endorsement of its default taste, a substitute for a brand system, or a measured performance win.
picks.version_note: Catalog downloads have their own pinned version; inspect before installing.
picks.reason: For visual exploration: choose a deliberate direction, then judge it against your own brand and audience.

longlist.decision: Shortlist skill creation and frontend exploration; inspect individual folder terms.
Shortlist debugging process. TDD remains interesting, but the existing native pilot tied and another task family has a disputed grader; no benefit claim.
Shortlist task-specific React performance; fresh small trial tied.
Strong browser-workflow candidate; browser permissions and runtime dominate, so compare on a real browser task separately.
Shortlist for a Remotion project; not a general film-quality ranking.
Domain shortlist for Hub operations. Training and hosted-job workflows require separate budget and execution checks.
Security specialist candidate. Detailed audit workflows and author test resources merit task-specific review; not blanket security certification.
Shortlist official platform workflow with concrete RLS traps and author evaluation description.
Official mobile-platform candidate. Relevant to an Expo job, not an all-purpose coding winner.
Official Workers and Agents platform candidate. Needs a real platform task to compare.
Azure-specific candidate with author SDK evaluation infrastructure; no independent across-domain efficacy claim.
Research-domain candidate with executable helpers, references and author test resources. Validate each scientific task and dependency separately.
Visual exploration candidate. The README explicitly identifies historical/demo material as inspiration rather than a runtime benchmark; do not rank that footage as measured skill quality.

ranking_basis: Editorial starting order for a general software builder: reusable debugging first, then specific performance work, skill evaluation and platform/media/design jobs. This is a source-reviewed recommendation, not a usage ranking or a measured effectiveness score. Choose the matching job, not the highest number.
